conditioningLevel.evidenceScope: Formula-only, exact-market DE INCI of record (sha256 7be31024…, direct Müller fetch), above-tail ranks 1–6; category-relative to the German drugstore rinse-out mask shelf.
conditioningLevel.rationale: Exactly one of the three §9.1 structural signals is satisfied, which §9.1 assigns to the moderate bucket by definition. This is a structurally minimal formula: one cationic species, two fatty alcohols, one silicone, no lipid. E2 ceiling: comparative structural intensity potential, not measured treatment performance.
evidenceSignals: STEARYL ALCOHOL (rank 2) — long-chain fatty alcohol in the top three, the one satisfied signal
STEARAMIDOPROPYL DIMETHYLAMINE (rank 3) — the only cationic species above the tail
BEHENTRIMONIUM METHOSULFATE (rank 11) — a second cationic, but BELOW tail_index 7
no non-fatty-alcohol lipid at any rank above the tail (Bis-Aminopropyl Dimethicone @5 is an R2 silicone, not an R4 lipid; Glutamic Acid @6 is a free amino acid)
CETYL ALCOHOL (rank 4) — a second fatty alcohol, but S2 asks for rank 2 or 3, which Stearyl Alcohol already satisfies; breadth of fatty alcohols is not a separate signal
conditioningLevel.derivation: S1 (≥2 distinct cationics above the tail) = NOT satisfied; one. S2 satisfied (Stearyl Alcohol @2). S3 (≥2 distinct non-fatty-alcohol lipids above the tail) = NOT satisfied; zero. Count = 1 of 3.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `moderate`: §9.1 assigns `moderate` to 'everything else, including exactly one satisfied signal'. Exactly one is satisfied.
`high` does not apply: it requires ≥2 of {S1,S2,S3}. Only S2 holds, and the second cationic that would have carried S1 sits four ranks below the marker.

`low` does not apply: it requires NONE of the three — specifically a single cationic species AND no fatty alcohol in the top three AND at most one lipid above the tail. The first and third conditions hold, but Stearyl Alcohol @2 defeats the second.

Confidence is `moderate` rather than `high` by the §9.1 rule itself: high confidence requires ≥2 signals pointing the same way, and only one is available — despite this being the cohort's best-sourced formula.
counterSignals: Polysorbate 20 @13, Disodium EDTA @12 and Methicone @23 are formulation infrastructure in the tail and earn nothing (lexicon family 10).
Biotin @22 earns zero credit on every property and is kept away from any hair-loss-adjacent language (G6).
limitations: A three-step concentration scale is at the edge of INCI support.
This is the one cohort product where source quality is excellent and the signal count is still thin — the scale's resolution, not the evidence, is the limit.

primaryFocus.rationale: Every special-purpose route fails, the moisture guard fails at zero cluster members, and the shine threshold fails its claim-corroboration leg. Step 6 is then reached with one genuine candidate: an amino silicone at rank 5 in a six-entry above-tail segment, which is a distinct silicone route beyond the ordinary mask base and is a dry-surface-control route. `general` was the close competitor. E2 ceiling: comparative smoothing potential, never weatherproof frizz control.
evidenceSignals: BIS-AMINOPROPYL DIMETHICONE (rank 5) — the only route above the tail beyond the conditioning base; amino silicones deposit preferentially on damaged, more anionic fibre regions (direction only, no numbers — Pr-2's circulating percentages are unverified)

primaryFocus.derivation: Step 1 baseline exclusion applied. Step 2: one M1 base observation plus one M1/M3 silicone observation. Step 3: `repair` blocked (no R5, bond_route none, and step 3 states explicitly that `bond_specific_support = claim_only` cannot set repair); `curl_support` blocked (single cationic, no polymer — slip is not distinctive); `color_care` blocked (no candidate, no positioning); `lightness` blocked (weight `moderate`, not `low`). Step 4 `moisture` blocked (zero humectants above the tail). Step 5 `shine` blocked (criteria 2 and 3 fail). Step 6 `smoothing` clears.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `smoothing`: step 6 requires dry surface control to be the clearest practical differentiator AND the architecture to extend materially beyond the ordinary mask base via a distinct silicone, substantive polymer, or substantial lipid route. The amino silicone at rank 5 is the only thing in this formula that is not base, so it is by construction both the clearest differentiator and the material extension.

`repair` does not apply, and this is the product's whole purpose in the cohort: the strongest bond positioning in the set produces no repair focus, because step 3 names 'generic repair naming' and 'bond_specific_support = claim_only' as things that cannot set `repair`.

`shine` does not apply: criterion 1 is arguably satisfied (an alignment-oriented amino silicone above the tail with a genuinely low lipid load — zero lipids above the tail), but criterion 2 fails because this same M1/M3 deposition is the sole optical basis, and criterion 3 fails outright for want of any gloss positioning. §9.5.4's own instruction in that case is to select `smoothing` and keep the claim as context — which is what was done.

`general` was the close competitor and lost narrowly. The argument for it: a single amino silicone in a thin formula is slender ground for a named focus, and step 6's 'clearest practical differentiator' is trivially satisfied when almost nothing else is present. The argument that won: §9.5.1 explicitly routes a `nonspecific` verdict to `smoothing` when the dry-surface route genuinely clears step 6, and an amino silicone at rank 5 of 6 above-tail entries is a real, distinct, non-baseline route. Confidence is held at `moderate` to record that this call could reasonably go the other way. See AP-07-SMOOTHINGVGENERAL.
counterSignals: The product makes no smoothing or anti-frizz claim, so the focus has no corroboration — permitted (positioning corroborates but never creates, and its absence does not block), but it means this focus rests on a single ingredient.

Consistency check performed against #06, which reaches `smoothing` on a dimethicone/dimethiconol pair at ranks 4–5. The two products reach the same focus on very different evidential strength; only confidence distinguishes them.
limitations: Amino silicones may support a comparative smoothing-on-damaged-hair reading; they do not raise repair_support_level, and no such upgrade was made.

focusCareVerdict.note: The repair direction is claim-only: no protein, no peptide, no named bond token, and an amino silicone that the standard and lexicon both name as an explicit non-qualifier. The moisture direction is unsupported: zero humectants above the tail. Generic conditioning distinguishes neither. §9.5.1's hard rule applied without exception — claims can never convert nonspecific formula evidence into a specialist focus, so 'Molecular Bond Repair' produced nothing. The verdict resolved to `smoothing` rather than `general` because the dry-surface route cleared step 6.

adjudicationPoints.title: §9.2's `low` weight anchor is effectively unreachable for a conventional mask emulsion
adjudicationPoints.body: The `low` anchor's second conjunct is 'no cetearyl-class fatty alcohol in the top three'. Lexicon family 2 states that a cetearyl-class alcohol at rank 2 is near-universal in this category, present in every calibration list checked, and that its presence 'therefore carries no signal at all'. The anchor thus conditions its lowest value on the absence of the category's single most universal ingredient at its most universal position. Across the twelve eligible cohort products, `low` was reached exactly once — by #02, which is not a conventional emulsion at all (water at rank 5, myristyl rather than cetearyl alcohol). This product makes the point sharply: a lipid-free above-tail segment with one cationic and one silicone is refused `low` on a fatty alcohol at rank 2. Candidate fix: replace the conjunct with a positive test on lipid load and cationic breadth, or require the fatty alcohol to be joined by a second fatty alcohol or a lipid before it blocks `low`.

adjudicationPoints.title: Step 6's `smoothing` bar is trivially met on a minimal formula, because 'clearest differentiator' is relative to what else is present
adjudicationPoints.body: Step 6 asks whether dry surface control is 'the clearest practical differentiator' and whether the architecture extends 'materially beyond the ordinary mask base'. On a six-entry above-tail segment containing exactly one non-base ingredient, both conjuncts are satisfied by construction — the single silicone is necessarily the clearest differentiator, because it is the only differentiator. The same test applied to #06 is met by a dimethicone/dimethiconol pair at ranks 4–5 in a rich formula, which is far stronger evidence for the same value. The standard currently has no way to distinguish 'smoothing because there is a real smoothing architecture' from 'smoothing because there is nothing else'. Candidate fix: add a floor — e.g. two distinct alignment-oriented species above the tail, or one within the first five ranks of the full list plus a corroborating claim — below which the fallback is `general`.
